methods.name: Wald test of nested linear models
methods.reference: lmtest::waldtest(test = 'F' | 'Chisq'); aod::wald.test (legacy reference, equal to the Chisq form)
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md, n = 100 and 200: statistics and RSS 1e-6 relative; p-values 1e-6 relative or 1e-12 absolute; counts exact

deviations.note: p2a uses n (RSS_r - RSS_u) / RSS_u; lmtest::waldtest(test = 'Chisq') and aod::wald.test give q F = (n - k) (RSS_r - RSS_u) / RSS_u: diag_wald_sim drop x2 0.01248835701 vs 0.01198882273, drop x2 and x3 514.9909496 vs 494.3913116; Grunfeld drop capital 83.23811806 vs 81.98954629

methods.name: HAC (kernel) covariance for OLS
methods.reference: sandwich::NeweyWest(lag = m, prewhite = FALSE) for Bartlett; sandwich::kernHAC(kernel =, bw = m, prewhite = FALSE, adjust = FALSE) for Parzen, Truncated, Tukey-Hanning
quantities: SE and covariance matrix: Bartlett (default and m = 4), Parzen, Truncated, Tukey-Hanning (m = 4)
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md, n = 100: coefficients 1e-8, SE and covariance entries 1e-6 relative; bandwidth exact

deviations.note: the QS kernel is truncated at the bandwidth: p2a 0.2284575999 / 0.1414513262 vs kernHAC(kernel = 'Quadratic Spectral', bw = 4, prewhite = FALSE, adjust = FALSE) 0.2300539548 / 0.1392422079 (kernhac_qs_bw4)

p2a's Bartlett bandwidth m weights lag j by 1 - j/(m + 1), i.e. NeweyWest(lag = m) = kernHAC(bw = m + 1) (pinned); kernHAC(kernel = 'Bartlett', bw = 4) is 0.2102028704 / 0.1464461033 (kernhac_bartlett_bw4) where p2a's m = 4 gives 0.2204664393 / 0.1429954779. Parzen, Truncated and Tukey-Hanning use j/m and match kernHAC(bw = m)
prewhiten = true fits a scalar AR(1) to the residuals: p2a 0.2908704449 / 0.3059566437 vs NeweyWest(lag = 4, prewhite = TRUE) 0.2858936714 / 0.1360607244 (neweywest_lag4_prewhite)

the default bandwidth is the fixed rule floor(4 (n/100)^(2/9)) = 4, not bwNeweyWest (2.513298742, bw_neweywest); there is no adjust = TRUE option: kernhac_*_bw4_adjust hold the adjusted values, e.g. Parzen 0.1977403619 / 0.1432982597 where p2a gives the unadjusted 0.1957529711 / 0.1418580397

methods.name: Driscoll-Kraay covariance for pooled OLS
methods.reference: sandwich::vcovPL(cluster = ~firm, order.by = ~time, kernel = 'Bartlett', lag = 2, adjust = FALSE); plm::vcovSCC(maxlag = 2) as a cross-check
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md, n = 200: coefficients 1e-8, SE 1e-6 relative; counts exact

deviations.quantity: Driscoll-Kraay SEs, covariance, t and p
deviations.note: scores are averaged within period and the meat is multiplied by T: p2a 0.02186774128 / 0.04533713058 = sqrt(T)/N (0.4472135955) x vcovPL 0.04889775602 / 0.1013769059 (vcovpl_lag2 = vcovscc_lag2). The legacy reference vcovPL(cluster = ~time, order.by = ~time) aggregates by firm, not period (legacy_vcovpl_cluster_time), and is not a Driscoll-Kraay value
Parzen, Tukey-Hanning and QS use the j/m bandwidth convention while vcovPL uses bw = lag + 1; not pinned, and no case holds a vcovPL value for them, so there is no R or p2a value to record
